solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Carey burnt inaccurate stories about a pilgrimage

definitions.text: Carey burnt inaccurate stories about a pilgrimage

indicators.note: an inaccurate version of the name has its letters set down wrongly, so they are rearranged

parts.note: stories are tales

explanation.surface: Someone called Carey has burnt a set of unreliable tales about a journey to a shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inaccurate' is the anagram signal. The whole clue then describes Chaucer's poem, whose stories are told by pilgrims travelling to Canterbury.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's medieval poem is a collection of stories told by pilgrims travelling to Canterbury.

clue.text: Actress, a foreign woman, and Hazel caught inside playing "Chase the Lady"

parts.note: Cher is the American singer and actress
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: playing about with the letters means they are rearranged

parts.note: femme is the French word for woman

explanation.surface: A list of a performer, a Frenchwoman and Hazel, caught up in a party game called Chase the Lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges HAZEL plus C to give CHEZLA. The pieces go in answer order: CHER, then CHEZLA, then FEMME.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase literally means look for the woman, rendered loosely as a hunt for the lady.

clue.text: Not one European found in the cell

indicators.note: the abbreviation is found sitting in the middle of the other word, so it goes inside

parts.note: not one means none
EUR is an abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Not a single European has turned up in the prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurone is a nerve cell, the British spelling of the body's signalling cell.

clue.text: City reporter batting for town

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a newspaper role standing in for reporter
in cricket the side batting is said to be in
a burgh is a Scottish town

explanation.surface: A city journalist is filling in at the crease for the local town side.
explanation.walkthrough: A BURGH is a Scottish chartered town; IN means batting, as in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Edinburgh is the capital city of Scotland.

clue.text: Blumenthal began to study food

indicators.note: where the name began means its first letter only

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it

explanation.surface: The celebrity chef Heston Blumenthal took up the study of food.
explanation.walkthrough: Heston Blumenthal is a famous British chef, which is why the clue feels like a cookery story.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is a staple food made from baked dough.

clue.text: Those who sanction arrest, maybe, if I am included

indicators.note: the two short words are included inside the shuffled letters
maybe suggests another possible arrangement of the word's letters

explanation.surface: Officials who approve an arrest wonder whether they themselves might be part of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' turns ARREST into RATERS, the shuffled word the pair of short words goes into; 'am' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To ratify is to sanction formally, so those who ratify are people giving official approval.

clue.text: Question of work in a short time

indicators.note: the work goes in the middle of the shortened word
short means the word for time loses its last letter

parts.note: a tick is a moment, a brief time
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A query about some job done in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: A TICK is a British word for a moment; cut short it is TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject or matter under discussion, as a question can be.

clue.text: Spooner is surprised by oaf on guard

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words swap theirs

parts.note: coo is a British exclamation of surprise
a lout is an oaf

explanation.surface: The clergyman is startled by a clumsy fellow on sentry duty.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of COO LOUT gives LOO KOUT, which sounds like the answer. 'Coo!' is a British cry of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookout is a person posted to keep watch, a sentry.

clue.text: Flag up traders' past sins

indicators.note: up means the letters are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Merchants' old misdeeds are being raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' tells you to rearrange the letters of TRADERS PAST SINS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stars and Stripes is the national flag of the United States.

clue.text: Universal credit was halved before housing academic

indicators.note: the first word houses the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
U is the film classification for universal

indicators.note: halved here leaves only the second half of the word

explanation.surface: A welfare payment was cut in half before it covered the housing costs.
explanation.walkthrough: Universal Credit is a British welfare benefit, which is why the surface reads like a news story; 'halved' keeps the second half of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudite means learned and scholarly, the qualities of an academic.

clue.text: A company one might knock back for food

indicators.note: knock back means the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to pat is to knock gently

explanation.surface: A business that someone might criticise for its catering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock back' looks like a phrase for drinking or rejecting, but 'back' reverses ACOIPAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapioca is a starchy food from cassava, often made into a pudding.

clue.text: Valley where nothing is contributed to hunt

indicators.note: the zero is contributed into the middle of the other word

parts.note: to comb an area is to hunt through it
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A valley where nobody adds anything to the local hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: A COOMB (or combe) is a word used in southern England for a short valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A coomb is a short valley or hollow on a hillside.

clue.text: Deserters who forecasted losing a retrial

indicators.note: losing tells you the short word is taken out of the letter pool
a retrial has the case tried again, so the letters are tried in another order

explanation.surface: Turncoats who predicted the outcome lose when their case is heard again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing a' removes A from FORECASTED and 'retrial' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Defectors abandon their side or country, which is what deserters do.

clue.text: Hated administrator gains most of farmland

parts.note: an exec is an executive, an administrator

indicators.note: most of means the word loses one letter

parts.note: arable land is farmland used for crops

explanation.surface: A loathed manager takes over most of the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops one A from ARABLE here, the first one, leaving RABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Execrable means abominable, so bad as to be loathed.

clue.text: Fortress partially in trouble; gets a beating

indicators.note: partially means only part of the word is used

parts.note: a bastion is a fortress or stronghold
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Someone stuck partly in a fortress and in difficulty takes a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' keeps only BAST of BASTION.
explanation.definitionFit: The bastinado is a punishment of beating the soles of the feet with a stick.

clue.text: Stayed home to get material

parts.note: sat means stayed put
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Someone stayed in to work on some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a smooth glossy fabric, a dress material.

clue.text: One might come into new family surroundings

definitions.text: One might come into new family surroundings

parts.words: One might come into new family surroundings
parts.note: a child joining a household through a parent's remarriage enters an unfamiliar family

explanation.surface: Someone moving into an unfamiliar household.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepchild is the child of one's spouse from an earlier relationship, joining a new family.

clue.text: Mutable echinoderm afflicted by parasite

indicators.note: the sea creature's words are afflicted by, or carry within them, the run of letters

explanation.surface: A changeable starfish-like creature plagued by a bloodsucking pest.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside mutabLE ECHinoderm: the words are 'afflicted by' it, so it is held within them.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a bloodsucking worm, the classic parasite.

clue.text: Design general increase

indicators.note: to design is to arrange anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plan to grow things across the board.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge is to make bigger, to increase in size.

clue.text: Mysteries coming back to haunt opponents of old money

parts.note: S and E, south and east, are opponents at the bridge table

indicators.note: coming back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: secrets are mysteries

explanation.surface: Unsolved puzzles return to trouble rivals over some ancient cash.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, South and East sit at adjacent sides and play against each other. SESTERCES are ancient Roman coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesterces were coins of ancient Rome, so old currency.

clue.text: 23 without one let out a laugh!

indicators.note: without means the letter is left out of the word

parts.note: the answer to 23 across is a word for singers
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A group of singers lacking a member lets out a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without one' takes I from the 23 answer to leave CHOR; 'out' rearranges LET as TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chortle is a gleeful chuckle, a kind of laugh.

clue.text: Doctors provided breast enhancements to cover it!

indicators.note: the padding covers the short word, enclosing it

parts.note: falsies are pads worn to enlarge the bust
if means provided that

explanation.surface: Doctors provide cosmetic breast work and then cover it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' looks like medics, but it is a verb meaning tampers with.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor something is to tamper with it, to fake it.

clue.text: Lumpy paint is not fit for purpose

indicators.note: lumpy paint has been churned up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lumpy paint is no good for the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or inappropriate for a task.

clue.text: Salvation Army leads graduate on a merry dance!

parts.note: an MBA is a business graduate

explanation.surface: Salvation Army members lead a business school alumnus on a wild chase.
explanation.walkthrough: To lead someone a merry dance is an idiom for giving them the run-around, hence the misleading surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The samba is a lively Brazilian dance.

clue.text: Singers about to go round the house

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the second, enclosing it

parts.note: cir. is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Singers about to go carolling round the houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is an organised group of singers.

clue.text: Mother's announced a Louisiana sweet wine

indicators.note: announced means the word is heard spoken

parts.note: Ma's, said in a British accent, sounds like Mars
LA is the postal abbreviation for Louisiana

explanation.surface: Mother announces she has a sweet wine from Louisiana.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech, MA'S and MARS sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsala is a fortified sweet wine from Sicily.

clue.text: Platform in the circus tent?

definitions.meaning: a platform at the head of the mainmast on a sailing ship
the big top of a circus could whimsically be called its ...

explanation.surface: A stage set up in the big top.
explanation.definitionFit: A maintop is the platform at the top of a sailing ship's lower mainmast.

clue.text: Are those for whom it is intended possibly considered least?

definitions.text: Are those for whom it is intended possibly considered least?

indicators.note: possibly suggests one possible rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A wry question whether voters, the audience for a candidate's speech, matter least to politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges CONSIDERED LEAST. The whole clue asks whether voters, for whom the speech is meant, are thought of least.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate's election address is a speech or leaflet aimed at voters.
